dedupe_keys.name: historical and simulated global production price and demand for copper cobalt and nickel 2001 2033 usgs

description: This U.S. Geological Survey data release gives the data behind every figure and table, the raw model output and the simulation parameters of the Nature Communications paper "Modeling interconnected minerals markets with multicommodity supply curves: examining the copper-cobalt-nickel system", covering historical and simulated global production, price and demand for copper, cobalt and nickel from 2001 to 2033. It was published on 18 June 2025 by John Ryter as a figure and table data archive of about 0.15 MB, a raw output archive of about 134 MB and XML metadata, downloadable and free under CC0 1.0, with global coverage. The ScienceBase page gives no further description of the model, so the scenario set, the mine-level detail and the file layout inside the archives are not stated on the page read. Caveats: simulated values depend on the paper's assumptions, and by-product links between the three metals mean results should be read with the paper. For simulation it gives market model outputs for copper, cobalt and nickel supply and price shock scenarios, useful to connect grid, battery and alloy manufacturing models to mineral market dynamics. Related catalogue records include the USGS world minerals outlook to 2029, the USGS global porphyry copper deposits and the EV battery cathode material flows.
